description: A risk committee chair must decide whether to grant a temporary covenant waiver to a renewable-energy borrower and set the waiver's protective conditions, with input from credit risk, legal, relationship management, and loan operations.

shared_context.S1: Solterra Energy's project-finance loan has a quarterly debt-service-coverage covenant of 1.20x, and the borrower reported a quarter-end ratio of 1.14x.
shared_context.S2: Solterra has requested a temporary waiver while its largest power-purchase customer completes a delayed payment.
shared_context.S3: The loan agreement permits the risk committee to grant a written covenant waiver with additional protective conditions.
shared_context.S4: Elena makes the binding decision. Under the committee's routine pre-decision procedure, Elena calls credit risk, legal, relationship management, and loan operations in that order; each function gives one concise report before Elena settles the waiver terms, and no function waits for another report before giving its own.

PF1.text: Grace confirmed in lender counsel's memo received this morning that any effective waiver must include both a signed no-default acknowledgment from Solterra and an express reservation of the bank's enforcement rights; the memo has not yet been attached to the committee packet.

PF2.text: Martin's stress review completed this week supports a waiver for exactly 60 days, but only with a 75-basis-point pricing step-up during the waiver period; those terms are in his working paper and have not been entered in the credit system.

PF3.text: Noah received a signed borrower commitment yesterday that Solterra can make a mandatory principal prepayment of exactly $350,000 within 10 calendar days, which makes the waiver acceptable under the relationship team's workout plan; he has not circulated the signed commitment.

PF4.text: Lina found while reviewing the servicing file this week that the loan's amended reporting protocol requires monthly compliance certificates throughout any covenant waiver; the protocol is not reflected in the current monitoring checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The covenant waiver must be granted for exactly 60 days.
The waiver must include a 75-basis-point pricing step-up.
The borrower must make a mandatory principal prepayment of exactly $350,000.
Monthly compliance certificates must be required during the waiver.
The written waiver must require a signed no-default acknowledgment.
The written waiver must expressly reserve the bank's enforcement rights.
The settlement must record commitments for the prepayment, pricing step-up, and monthly compliance certificates.

content_checks.C8: any(('350000' in c['detail'] or '$350,000' in c['detail']) and 'prepayment' in c['detail'] for c in commitments) and any('75' in c['detail'] and ('basis-point' in c['detail'] or 'basis point' in c['detail']) and 'pricing' in c['detail'] for c in commitments) and any('monthly compliance certificate' in c['detail'] or 'monthly compliance certificates' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Without PF1, the settlement can omit both the no-default acknowledgment and the enforcement-rights reservation; PF1 changes no_default_acknowledgment_required and enforcement_rights_reserved from false to true and supplies the cited legal basis.
Without PF2, the public request gives no exact protective timetable or pricing adjustment; PF2 changes waiver_period_days to exactly 60 and pricing_step_up_basis_points to exactly 75.

Without PF3, the covenant breach supports declining the waiver rather than approving it; PF3 changes waiver_granted to true and mandatory_prepayment_usd to exactly 350000 while supplying the mandatory-prepayment commitment.

Without PF4, the settlement has no basis for requiring monthly certificates; PF4 changes monthly_compliance_certificates from false or unspecified to true and supplies the monthly-compliance-reporting commitment.
